His history studies enhanced his critical perspective, enabling him to produce insightful analyses that extended to submissions for national outlets like Crawdaddy! and Rolling Stone even before graduation; this academic grounding in structured argumentation profoundly shaped his later rock journalism.

While still a student, he began writing music reviews for the campus newspaper The Justice and soon contributed to national publications, marking his transition from an avid fan immersed in the burgeoning counterculture of the mid-1960s to a professional critic. This shift occurred amid the explosive growth of rock music as a cultural force, driven by the psychedelic and soul scenes, which Landau analyzed with a scholarly rigor informed by his academic background.
